_source.origin: NASA LIS/OTD lightning climatology (lightning.nsstc.nasa.gov) and Albrecht et al. 2016 'Where are the lightning hotspots on Earth?' (doi:10.1175/BAMS-D-14-00193.1).
_source.license: NASA: public domain; Albrecht: published research
_source.notes: Hotspot locations from NASA LIS/OTD satellite climatology.

hotspot.name: Lake Maracaibo (Catatumbo Lightning)
hotspot.notes: World's highest lightning density; 297 storm days/year; 28 flashes/min

hotspot.name: Congo Basin
hotspot.notes: 2nd highest flash rate globally; tropical convection over dense forest

hotspot.name: Kifuka, DR Congo
hotspot.notes: Former record holder: 158 flashes/km²/year; mountainous tropical

hotspot.name: Central Florida (Lightning Alley)
hotspot.notes: US lightning capital; sea breeze convergence; ~80 days/year

hotspot.name: Río de la Plata Basin
hotspot.notes: Intense MCS thunderstorms; among world's most severe

hotspot.name: Kampala, Uganda
hotspot.notes: ~240 thunderstorm days/year; Lake Victoria convergence effects

hotspot.name: Northern Colombia Andes
hotspot.notes: Andean orographic lift creates persistent afternoon storms

hotspot.name: Darwin, Northern Territory
hotspot.notes: Hector the Convector; daily storms over Tiwi Islands, Nov-Mar

hotspot.name: Paraguay/Southern Brazil
hotspot.notes: Subtropical convective storms; high flash density corridor

hotspot.name: Gulf of Mexico Coast
hotspot.notes: Warm Gulf moisture + frontal systems; 50-60 storms/year

hotspot.name: Himalayan Foothills (Nepal)
hotspot.notes: Orographic monsoon storms; extremely dangerous lightning

hotspot.name: West African Sahel
hotspot.notes: Intense MCS supercells during monsoon season; large hail
